headline: Oil prices fluctuate amid uncertainty over possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz
summary: Crude oil prices showed little movement on August 10 after erasing earlier gains. Optimism over negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was offset by Iran's position that US demands must be met first.
why: Brent and WTI are the benchmark crude grades, and the Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of seaborne oil, so any disruption there feeds directly into global energy prices.
why_moved: Negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz were presented as uncertain, with Iran setting conditions, which left crude prices without a clear direction after an earlier rally was erased.
